GPT-5.6 parses the team's uploaded brand guide PDF against extracted frames to generate event rules (e.g., 'HEX #2D2D2D must occupy >30% of non-sky pixels'). A discrete event simulation clock ticks through each frame of generated video candidates; at each tick, Codex executes a Python script calling fal-hosted computer vision endpoints to measure state variables. The simulation log records timestamps where constraints are violated, producing a per-video compliance trace and a time-weighted compliance score.

Below each video, a live simulation event log highlights exact timestamps of guideline violations (e.g., 'Logo absent at 2.3s'), while a stacked bar shows cumulative time spent in-compliance vs. out-of-compliance. The creative lead clicks a single 'Generate Compliance Report' button to produce a PDF with frame grabs of every violation across all candidates, instantly shareable with the client.
ideas.visible_transformation: A chaotic folder of 15 AI-generated product ads transforms into a scored, filterable comparison grid where the team objectively eliminates 12 candidates in 90 seconds because the simulation exposes that the brand's cobalt blue appears only 8% of the time instead of the required 35%.

ideas.working_title: StyleForge: Counterfactual Style Injection for Non-Generic Anime
ideas.primary_user: Solo generative media artists creating anime-style short films
ideas.painful_workflow: They want to produce high-quality anime with unique, personal art styles, but the default model outputs look generic. To achieve a distinctive aesthetic, they must manually post-process frames or write extremely complex single-prompt style descriptions that still drift.
ideas.current_workaround: Artists spend hours in Photoshop drawing over individual frames to impose their line-art or color-choice preferences. Others paste 500-word style prompts into the generator, hoping three adjectives survive, then accept the generic output and pretend the 'muted, desaturated cel-shading with weighted ink contours at 45-degree hatching' was intentional.
ideas.core_computation: GPT-5.6 analyzes the artist's reference pack (character sheets, background art, color scripts) and constructs a causal DAG linking style attributes to visual outcomes. Codex then implements an estimation engine that, for each generated frame, computes a style-propensity score by matching observed features against the reference set. For any frame flagged as 'generic' (low estimated treatment effect from the style reference), the system formulates a counterfactual: what would this frame look like if the style treatment had been fully applied? GPT-5.6 generates a targeted inpainting or control signal prompt correction via the fal API—adjusting only the deviating attributes (e.g., 'thicken line weight by estimated delta of 1.4x')—and re-submits the frame for targeted regeneration. This avoids full re-generation and converges toward the style with fewer API calls.
ideas.last_mile_action: The artist drags their style reference folder (3-10 images) onto the interface. They paste their base scene prompt and click 'Generate with Style Treatment.' A side-by-side viewer shows pairs of frames: the generic 'control' output on the left, the style-treated output on the right. Below each pair, a causal-style report reads 'Line weight confidence: 92% match to reference (up from 43%), color saturation delta applied: -22%.' The artist can adjust sliders to manually weight specific style attributes (line weight, palette adherence, shading gradient) and the counterfactual engine re-calculates treatment effects in real-time, selectively regenerating only the adjusted attributes.
ideas.visible_transformation: A flat, generic anime clip of a samurai in a forest becomes visually indistinguishable from the artist's personal sketchbook style—heavy ink contours, a restricted palette of ochre-vermillion-teal, and stylized leaf silhouettes—without the artist ever opening Photoshop or guessing at prompt engineering.
ideas.sponsor_dependency: GPT-5.6 reasoning and Codex-built evaluation harness
ideas.technical_risk: quality of the fixed evaluation fixture
ideas.why_now: Anime is an explicit Generative Media Track theme, and 'generic anime characters' is flagged as a high-collision risk. The hackathon offers Grok Imagine and Kling via fal API, which could be orchestrated with style-reference injection to escape the generic look—aligning with the 'multi-model synergy beyond chaining' underexplored area.
ideas.killer_demo: The presenter creates a folder with three images: the artist's original character design sheet, a background color key, and a 1-second clip of 'generic forest anime.' They type 'samurai walks through bamboo forest, long lens, cinematic' and hit generate on a vanilla fal endpoint—the output is clean but plastic-looking. Then they switch to StyleForge, drag the same reference folder, paste the identical prompt, and click 'Generate with Style Treatment.' The tool shows a cascading estimate: 'Estimated style adherence: 37% on control frame.' A progress bar appears as Codex iterates counterfactual corrections. Within a minute, the treated frame appears side-by-side: visible ink lines now mimic the artist's brush weight, the colors match the restricted palette, and the leaf shapes echo the background key. The causal report shows a final treatment effect of 89% style match (baseline: 37%). The presenter exports the treated clip directly to a project timeline.
ideas.hard_to_fake_advantage: Prompt-chaining tools simply feed the output of one model into another and hope style emerges. StyleForge frames style adherence as a causal estimation problem with measurable deltas per visual attribute. Because it only re-generates attributes where the estimated treatment effect is low, it achieves style convergence with fewer API credits and produces a quantifiable style-match percentage—neither of which is possible with prompt engineering alone.

ideas.primary_user: AI-native filmmakers producing multi-scene narrative shorts (opp-001).
ideas.painful_workflow: Struggling to maintain consistent character appearance, lighting, and world details across every new shot. Wasting hackathon time on manual prompt re-entry instead of directing the story.
ideas.current_workaround: Copy-pasting lengthy style descriptors into every generation prompt and hoping for visual coherence; manually curating the least-bad outputs.
ideas.imported_mechanism: Statistical Process Control for Anomaly Detection (M2).
ideas.core_computation: A Python-based pre-processor that parses a filmmaker's script (Final Draft or Fountain format) to extract scene headings and character appearances. It builds a 'Style Bible' data structure with visual parameters (e.g., `character_coat_hex`, `scene_lighting_temp_K`). As the filmmaker iterates through shots, GPT-5.6 analyzes the generated sequence of prompts and their corresponding outputs (via the fal API) to detect 'style drift' using a multivariate CUSUM control chart. When a statistically significant deviation in a visual metric is detected, Codex generates a real-time, minimal corrective injection (e.g., 'cinematic lighting, deep cyan shadows, 3200K warmth') that is appended to the next prompt in the pipeline, bringing the process back into a state of statistical control for visual consistency.
ideas.last_mile_action: The system automatically appends a corrective style injection to the next shot's prompt in the filmmaker's queue, ensuring visual coherence, and logs the detected drift metric and correction for post-production review.
ideas.visible_transformation: A filmmaker writes a script containing three scenes with a character named 'EVA'. They highlight EVA's portrait and define 'cyan coat'. The tool sequences five generated shots. After shot 3, the filament color in the coat has shifted from #00FFFF to #1A6B7A. The SPC module detects this drift, alerts the user, and automatically corrects the prompt for shot 4 with '+ cyan color #00FFFF', reverting the coat color. The before/after shows the coat's RGB histogram variance reduced from 8% to 1.5% across all five shots.
ideas.sponsor_dependency: GPT-5.6 reasoning and Codex-built evaluation harness
ideas.technical_risk: quality of the fixed evaluation fixture
ideas.why_now: Anime is an explicit Generative Media Track theme, and 'generic anime characters' is flagged as a high-collision risk. The hackathon offers Grok Imagine and Kling via fal API, which could be orchestrated with style-reference injection to escape the generic look—aligning with the 'multi-model synergy beyond chaining' underexplored area.
ideas.killer_demo: The demo begins with a director loading a script. They define a Style Bible for the character 'EVA' (cyan coat). The tool generates a five-shot sequence. Mid-sequence, we deliberately see the coat color drifting to teal. An on-screen SPC chart flags the drift with a red dot violating the CUSUM limit. The system automatically injects a correction into the prompt for the next shot. The final shot's coat is visibly identical to the first. The video ends with a split-screen variance histogram: 8.2% baseline variance (without correction) vs. 1.5% with the SPC-based correction system.
ideas.hard_to_fake_advantage: Unlike one-shot prompt generators, this system actively monitors the generative process as a manufacturing line, using SPC to detect and automatically correct for drift. This closes the loop between creation and quality assurance in a way that static constraint propagation cannot.

ideas.primary_user: Developer-track participants building AI-video tools under extreme time pressure (opp-002).
ideas.painful_workflow: Must demonstrate a polished, working tool in a 3-minute demo, but any real-time AI generation glitch or latency spike can ruin the recording and waste precious 72-hour development time.
ideas.current_workaround: Recording demos a dozen times and praying for no failures, or avoiding live generation entirely by faking it with pre-rendered video clips.
ideas.core_computation: An SDK middleware that defines a 'glitchless demo' constraint satisfaction problem. The variables are the set of all cacheable AI outputs for a demo flow (e.g., `scene_1_shot_2`, `loading_loop`). Domains are the acceptable runtime metrics (e.g., `latency_ms: [500,3000]`, `resolution: [720,1080]`). The constraints are the desired visual continuity. Before the demo, Codex constructs a complete fallback state-space representing a valid demo arc. During the live demo, if a primary fal API call fails (violating a runtime constraint), GPT-5.6 solves the constraint graph in real-time to select the most contextually coherent pre-rendered fallback that maintains narrative and visual flow, arc-consistently blending it into the playback stream.
ideas.last_mile_action: A developer's tool, upon detecting a real-time generation failure, seamlessly crossfades to the pre-computed, constraint-satisfying optimal fallback clip and schedules an automatic retry of the primary model connection.
ideas.visible_transformation: In a live coding demo, a developer deliberately throttles their network. Their app attempts to generate a new video segment. The system's overlay shows 'primary request failed – constraint violated: latency > 5000ms'. Instantly, the screen cross-dissolves from a buffering icon to a previously generated, context-perfect clip of a character walking. The demo continues without stutter, and a subtle 'router active' icon appears. The demo log then shows the constraint solver selecting the fallback with a 0.98 similarity match to the intended shot.
ideas.sponsor_dependency: GPT-5.6 reasoning and Codex-built evaluation harness
ideas.technical_risk: quality of the fixed evaluation fixture
ideas.why_now: The hackathon's judging criteria heavily weights storytelling (35%) and visual consistency under technical capability, while fal's Assets system is purpose-built for reusable character identity but remains underutilized without automated prompt-chain tooling.
ideas.killer_demo: A developer live-demos their AI storyboard tool using the fal API. They click 'Generate Next Shot.' As the generation fires, they simulate a severe network throttle. The UI shows a real-time metric: 'Constraint Violation: Latency 8200ms [Limit: 4000ms]'. Instead of an error, a perfectly matched, pre-rendered fallback clip of the same character in a similar pose crossfades in. The demo voiceover states, 'And the Glitchless Router just switched to the constraint-solving backup.' After the demo, they show the console log with the arc-consistency solver's decision tree, proving it wasn't a pre-scripted fake.
ideas.hard_to_fake_advantage: Applies formal Constraint Satisfaction methods to create an optimal, invisible safety net for live demos, generating a contextually perfect fallback state-space rather than just a single static video backup. This guarantees narrative coherence during failure, which a simple try-catch or buffer cannot.
